subject: Acme Corp POC - Integration & Success Criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Acme Corp POC - Integration & Success Criteria

Hi Alex / Sofia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed plan so we’re aligned going into the POC: 

High-level objective:
- Validate Redwood inference integration for Acme’s in-product assistant: throughput, latency under your typical session sizes, and end-to-end quality for your top 3 intents.

Proposed success criteria (more details attached in POC-Success-Criteria.xlsx):
- Latency: median request-to-first-token < 300ms for 512-token context at 8 concurrent users.
- Throughput: sustained 100 reqs/min for the POC endpoint without queueing above target SLO.
- Quality: intent precision > 85% on your 150-sample eval set (we’ll use the eval harness you shared).
- Stability: no more than 2% error rate over 72-hour soak test.

POC scope and timeline:
- Duration: 4 weeks (target start: 2026-04-06).
- Week 0: provisioning + integration (API keys, test data, sample SDK run).
- Week 1-2: run functional tests + small-scale load tests.
- Week 3: soak tests + quality evals.
- Week 4: results review + success sign-off / next steps.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Marissa (commercial lead), Lukas (integration lead / engineer on record), Neha (solutions PM).
- Acme: Alex (product), Sofia (engineering lead).

Integration notes / asks for the kickoff:
- We’ll provide an SDK sample repo for Node + Python and a streaming example (token-level streaming over websockets/HTTP2).
- Please share: a sandbox API key request contact, VPN or IP allowlist if needed, test dataset (150 eval samples) and a representative traffic profile (avg ctx length, avg tokens per response).
- For tool calling: confirm whether the assistant will invoke internal tools (search, DB lookups). If yes, we’ll include a stubbed tool-calling flow in the SDK.

Attachments: POC-Success-Criteria.xlsx, Redwood-POC-Plan.pdf

Next steps (action items):
1) Alex — confirm success criteria & target start date by EOD Wed (2026-03-25).
2) Marissa/Neha — provision sandbox API + share SDK link and integration checklist by Tue (2026-03-24).
3) Lukas — prepare initial sample integration docs and a GitHub repo stub.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Corp POC - Integration & Success Criteria

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary, this is very helpful. We’re aligned on the high-level objective and the 4-week timeline looks good. A few clarifications / confirmations from our side: 

Success criteria notes:
- Latency: the 300ms median for 512-token context is acceptable as a target; we’ll confirm internal measurements during week 1.
- Quality: we’ll share the 150-sample eval set by tomorrow. We’ll want to add one additional metric: hallucination rate on knowledge lookup flows (we’ll provide labels for that).

Environment & access:
- We’ll need a sandbox API key and the sample SDK repo. Also, we require IP allowlist for inbound connections — I’ll send our infra team contact (cc Sofia) to coordinate.

Tool calling:
- Yes, our assistant will call two internal tools during the POC (product catalog lookup, and order history). For the POC we can provide stubbed REST endpoints; we’d like the SDK example to show the tool-calling flow and secure token exchange.

Owners on our side:
- Product: Alex (me) — success criteria & acceptance
- Engineering: Sofia — integration and infra

Procurement / PO:
- I’ll start the PO process; procurement asked for a PO template/estimate. If we can get the estimated committed hours/credits for the 4-week POC, that’ll help speed approvals.

I’ll confirm the start date by Friday but leaning toward the week of April 6.

Cheers,
Alex
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp

Neha

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Alex Carter <alex.carter@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Acme Corp POC - Integration & Success Criteria

Hi all —

Quick engineering plan / checklist for the POC integration (ETA: initial repo + README by 2026-03-26):
1) SDKs: create example clients (Node + Python) that call our REST endpoints and demonstrate streaming using EventSource + chunked HTTP.
2) API routes: provide a POC endpoint (POST /v1/poc/generate) with the following patterns:
   - Non-streaming: standard JSON response with final output.
   - Streaming: chunked responses with token metadata header fields for latency measurement.
3) Tool calling: include an example of register/invoke tool pattern where the assistant emits a tool call (JSON schema) and Redwood forwards to the stub endpoint; sample exchange will show secure bearer token swap.
4) Auth & network: instructions for API key provisioning, IP allowlist config, and HMAC-signed webhook examples for tool callbacks.
5) Load test harness: small k6 script and a suggested attack surface (concurrency / payload sizes) so Acme can reproduce throughput.

I’ll post the initial repo here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/acme-poc and attach the README to the Drive folder. If Acme wants websockets instead of chunked HTTP for streaming, we can add a socket example.

Lukas
Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
